results.question: At the peak hour of the day (Sydney time), how many online orders do we get in total?
results.sql: SELECT peak_hour.hour_of_day, count(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM (SELECT extract(hour from o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') AS hour_of_day, count(o.order_id) AS cnt FROM orders o WHERE o.sales_channel = 'online' AND o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY cnt DESC LIMIT 1) peak_hour JOIN orders o ON extract(hour from o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') = peak_hour.hour_of_day WHERE o.sales_channel = 'online' AND o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY peak_hour.hour_of_day
results.answer: Your peak online ordering hour in Sydney time is 8:00 PM, during which you received a total of 1,232 orders. This total accumulates all orders placed at that specific hour across the entire dataset from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026.
results.assumptions: Data covers 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30. Peak hour determined across all online orders in the entire dataset using Australia/Sydney time, and showing the total order count accumulated during that specific hour of the day across all days.

results.question: How much revenue did our dresses bring in?
results.sql: SELECT sum(l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) AS dress_revenue FROM order_lines l JOIN orders o ON l.order_id = o.order_id JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND lower(p.product_type) = 'dress'
results.answer: Your dresses brought in a gross revenue of $542,989.65 across all time. This total includes line revenue from non-voided orders of dresses while excluding custom sales.

results.question: What is our overall gross profit margin?
results.sql: SELECT round(sum((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1 - v.cost * l.quantity) * 100.0 / sum((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1), 2) AS overall_gross_profit_margin_percent FROM orders o JOIN order_lines l ON o.order_id = l.order_id JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND v.cost IS NOT NULL
results.answer: Your overall gross profit margin is 58.32% for all time. This calculation is based on ex-GST revenue to compare against your unit costs, and it excludes voided orders and any variants with missing cost data.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: overall gross profit margin for all time (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30), excluding variants with NULL cost and voided orders. Revenue is converted to ex-GST by dividing by 1.1 to compare against ex-GST unit cost.

results.question: What are our top 5 products by gross profit?
results.sql: SELECT p.title AS product_title, sum(l.quantity) AS units_sold, round(sum((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1 - v.cost * l.quantity), 2) AS gross_profit FROM products p JOIN variants v USING (product_id) JOIN order_lines l USING (variant_id) JOIN orders o USING (order_id) WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND p.status <> 'custom' AND v.cost IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY gross_profit DESC LIMIT 5
results.answer: Your top 5 products by gross profit are the One-Piece Swimsuit with $165,884.48 (4,043 units), the Shirt Dress with $130,441.22 (1,492 units), the Straw Hat with $108,854.01 (3,619 units), the High-Rise Jeans with $104,531.12 (1,295 units), and the Wool Coat with $89,912.11 (828 units). These figures cover sales from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026, and exclude products with missing cost data or custom sales.
results.assumptions: Interpreting gross profit as revenue after discounts (ex-GST, by dividing line totals by 1.1) minus total cost (variants.cost * quantity). Variants with NULL cost and custom sales are excluded. Data covers 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30.

results.question: What is our net revenue after refunds?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(COALESCE(gross_rev, 0) - COALESCE(total_ref, 0), 2) AS net_revenue, ROUND(COALESCE(gross_rev, 0), 2) AS gross_revenue, ROUND(COALESCE(total_ref, 0), 2) AS total_refunds FROM (SELECT SUM(total) AS gross_rev FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided') o CROSS JOIN (SELECT SUM(r.amount) AS total_ref FROM refunds r JOIN orders o USING (order_id) WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided') r
results.answer: Your net revenue after refunds across all time is $3,205,298.79. This is based on a gross revenue of $3,321,930.71 minus $116,631.92 in total refunds. This calculation covers all non-voided orders from October 1, 2025, through September 30, 2026.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: What is our net revenue after refunds across all time (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30)? Net revenue is calculated as gross revenue from non-voided orders minus refund amounts associated with non-voided orders.

results.question: What percentage of orders had a refund?

results.answer: Out of all your non-orders, 5.7% had at least one refund between October 2025 and September 2026. This percentage is based on all available data from that one-year period.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: What percentage of non-voided orders had at least one refund, using all available data (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: Which product has had the most units refunded, and how many?
results.sql: SELECT p.title AS product_title, sum(rl.quantity) AS units_refunded FROM refund_lines rl JOIN refunds r USING (refund_id) JOIN order_lines ol USING (order_line_id) JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = r.order_id JOIN variants v USING (variant_id) JOIN products p USING (product_id) WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY units_refunded DESC LIMIT 1
results.answer: The product with the most units refunded is the One-Piece Swimsuit, with 165 units refunded. This data covers the period from October 1, 2025, through September 30, 2026, and excludes any refunds tied to voided orders.
results.assumptions: Data period: 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30. Excluded refunds on voided orders. Counted units refunded per product title.

results.question: How many different customers have placed an order?
results.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT customer_id) AS number_of_unique_customers FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND customer_id IS NOT NULL
results.answer: A total of 2,909 different customers have placed an order across the entire data period. This count excludes guest orders where a customer profile was not registered.
results.assumptions: Counting unique customers who placed at least one non-voided order across the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Guest orders (where customer_id is NULL) are excluded, as many are in-store purchases without a registered profile.

results.question: What percentage of orders were placed by guests with no customer account?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN customer_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS guest_order_percentage, COUNT(*) AS total_orders, SUM(CASE WHEN customer_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS guest_orders FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
results.answer: Guests without a customer account placed 22.47% of your orders across the data period. Out of a total of 17,340 non-voided orders, 3,896 were made by guests. This analysis covers the entire recorded timeframe from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as the percentage of non-voided orders placed by guests (where customer_id is NULL) across the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: What was our revenue in each of the last 3 months?
results.sql: SELECT to_char(created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney', 'YYYY-MM') AS month, round(sum(total)::numeric, 2) AS gross_revenue FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') >= (date_trunc('month', '2026-09-30'::date AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') - interval '2 months') AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') < (date_trunc('month', '2026-09-30'::date AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') + interval '1 month') GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 ASC
results.answer: Your gross revenue for the last three months was $342,251.10 in July, $282,129.97 in August, and $278,068.87 in September. These figures exclude voided orders and cover data up to 30 September 2026.
results.assumptions: Data covers up to 30 September 2026 (treated as today). 'Last 3 months' refers to July 2026, August 2026, and September 2026. Revenue is gross revenue (orders.total) excluding voided orders.

results.question: How did revenue during the EOFY sale (19 June to 5 July 2026) compare to the same number of days immediately before it?
results.sql:
WITH eofy_period AS (
  SELECT 
    'EOFY Sale (19 Jun - 5 Jul)' AS period,
    sum(total) AS gross_revenue,
    count(order_id) AS order_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
    AND created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' >= '2026-06-19 00:00:00'
    AND created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' < '2026-07-06 00:00:00'
),
before_period AS (
  SELECT 
    'Pre-EOFY (2 Jun - 18 Jun)' AS period,
    sum(total) AS gross_revenue,
    count(order_id) AS order_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
    AND created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' >= '2026-06-02 00:00:00'
    AND created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' < '2026-06-19 00:00:00'
)
SELECT period, round(gross_revenue::numeric, 2) AS gross_revenue, order_count FROM eofy_period
UNION ALL
SELECT period, round(gross_revenue::numeric, 2) AS gross_revenue, order_count FROM before_period;
results.answer: Revenue during the EOFY sale was higher than the preceding 17 days, bringing in $246,002.91 across 1,240 orders compared to $186,171.83 from 794 orders before the sale. This comparison assumes that gross revenue from non-paid or voided orders is accurately excluded and that both 17-day periods experience similar baseline traffic.
results.assumptions: Comparing the 17-day EOFY sale period (19 June to 5 July 2026 inclusive) against the immediately preceding 17 days (2 June to 18 June 2026). Revenue means gross revenue from non-voided orders.

results.question: Which 3 products have sold the fewest units?
results.sql: SELECT p.title AS product_title, sum(l.quantity) AS units_sold FROM products p JOIN variants v ON p.product_id = v.product_id JOIN order_lines l ON v.variant_id = l.variant_id JOIN orders o ON l.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND p.status <> 'custom' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY units_sold ASC, p.title ASC LIMIT 3
results.answer: The three products that sold the fewest units between 1 October 2025 and 30 September 2026 are the Rash Vest with 221 units, the Maxi Dress with 232 units, and the Knit Midi Dress with 253 units. These figures combine sales across all variants of each product and exclude custom sales and voided orders.
results.assumptions: Data covers 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30. Excludes custom sales (status = 'custom') and voided orders. Ranked by total units sold across all variants of each product.

results.question: How many customers have placed 3 or more orders?
results.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL AND financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING count(order_id) >= 3) t
results.answer: A total of 1,640 identified customers have placed 3 or more non-voided orders. This count is based on all-time data and strictly includes registered customers, meaning any guest orders made without an account were excluded from the total.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: How many identified customers have placed 3 or more non-voided orders across all time (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Guest orders (customer_id IS NULL) are excluded.

results.question: On average, how many days after the order are refunds issued?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.created_at - o.created_at)) / 86400.0)::numeric, 1) AS average_days_to_refund FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided'
results.answer: On average, refunds are issued 18.5 days after an order is placed. This calculation is based on non-voided orders and covers the period from October 1, 2025, through September 30, 2026.
results.assumptions: Calculated the difference in days between the order creation timestamp (orders.created_at) and the refund creation timestamp (refunds.created_at) for non-voided orders. Data covers 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30.

results.question: How much revenue came from orders that used a discount?
results.sql: SELECT round(sum(total)::numeric, 2) AS gross_revenue_with_discounts FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND discount_id IS NOT NULL;
results.answer: You earned $944,363.46 in gross revenue from orders that used a discount between October 1, 2025, and September 30, 2026. This total includes all non-voided orders where a discount was applied.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as gross revenue (orders.total) from all non-voided orders across the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30) that had a discount applied (discount_id IS NOT NULL).

results.question: Which colour sold the most units in winter (June to August 2026), and how many?
results.sql: SELECT v.color, SUM(l.quantity) AS units_sold FROM order_lines l JOIN orders o ON l.order_id = o.order_id JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND (o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') >= '2026-06-01 00:00:00' AND (o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') < '2026-09-01 00:00:00' AND v.color IS NOT NULL GROUP BY v.color ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 1
results.answer: Camel sold the most units in winter 2026 with a total of 1,050 units sold. This data covers the period from June 1, 2026, to August 31, 2026, and excludes any voided orders.
results.assumptions: Winter 2026 defined as June 1, 2026 to August 31, 2026 in Australia/Sydney time. Excluded voided orders.

results.question: Compare weekend revenue with weekday revenue.
results.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN EXTRACT(ISODOW FROM o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') IN (6, 7) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END AS day_type, round(sum(o.total), 2) AS gross_revenue, count(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM orders o WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY gross_revenue DESC
results.answer: Weekdays brought in more money than weekends, with weekdays generating $2,147,980.22 across 11,153 orders compared to $1,173,950.49 from 6,187 orders on weekends. This comparison covers all available data from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2025, using local Sydney time and excludes any voided orders.
results.assumptions: Comparing weekend revenue against weekday revenue across all available data (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30) using Australia/Sydney local time to define weekends (Saturday and Sunday) and weekdays (Monday through Friday). Voided orders are excluded.

results.question: What is the best-selling product in each product type?
results.sql: WITH ranked_products AS (SELECT p.product_type, p.title AS product_title, sum(l.quantity) AS units_sold, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY lower(p.product_type) ORDER BY sum(l.quantity) DESC) AS rn FROM products p JOIN variants v ON p.product_id = v.product_id JOIN order_lines l ON v.variant_id = l.variant_id JOIN orders o ON l.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND p.status <> 'custom' GROUP BY p.product_type, p.title) SELECT product_type, product_title AS best_selling_product, units_sold FROM ranked_products WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY units_sold DESC;
results.answer: The best-selling products by units sold across your product types are the One-Piece Swimsuit for Swimwear with 4,043 units, the Straw Hat for accessories with 3,619 units, the Linen Wrap Skirt for Skirt with 1,804 units, the Shirt Dress for Dress with 1,492 units, the Ribbed Tank for Top with 1,395 units, the High-Rise Jeans for Pants with 1,295 units, the Wool Coat for Outerwear with 828 units, and the Merino Crew Jumper for Knitwear with 526 units. This covers all available data from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026, and excludes voided orders and custom products.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: Best-selling product (by units sold) for each product type across all available data (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30), excluding voided orders and custom products. Product types are grouped case-insensitively.

results.question: How many orders contained more than one unit in total?
results.sql: SELECT count(*) AS order_count FROM (SELECT o.order_id FROM orders o JOIN order_lines l ON o.order_id = l.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY o.order_id HAVING sum(l.quantity) > 1) t
results.answer: You had 8,908 orders that contained more than one unit in total between October 1, 2025, and September 30, 2026. This count is based on all non-voided orders where the combined quantity across all order lines for a single order was greater than one.
results.assumptions: Data covers 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30 (all time). Excluded voided orders. Counted orders where the sum of quantities across all order lines for that order is greater than 1.

results.question: For each store location show the number of orders, units sold and revenue
results.sql: WITH order_summary AS (SELECT location_id, count(order_id) AS order_count, sum(total) AS gross_revenue FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY location_id), line_summary AS (SELECT o.location_id, sum(ol.quantity) AS units_sold FROM orders o JOIN order_lines ol ON o.order_id = ol.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY o.location_id) SELECT l.name AS location_name, l.type AS location_type, coalesce(os.order_count, 0) AS order_count, coalesce(ls.units_sold, 0) AS units_sold, round(coalesce(os.gross_revenue, 0)::numeric, 2) AS gross_revenue FROM locations l LEFT JOIN order_summary os ON l.location_id = os.location_id LEFT JOIN line_summary ls ON l.location_id = ls.location_id ORDER BY gross_revenue DESC;
results.answer: Your sales are led by the Online Store with 10,667 orders, 20,372 units sold, and $2,070,833.88 in revenue. The Surry Hills Boutique followed with 4,036 orders, 7,533 units sold, and $755,981.28, while the Newtown Boutique recorded 2,637 orders, 4,966 units sold, and $495,115.55. These figures exclude any voided orders and calculate orders separately from units sold to prevent double-counting.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: For each store location show the number of orders, units sold and revenue. Order counts and revenue are calculated from orders alone, and units sold from order_lines alone, joined via CTEs to avoid inflation. Voided orders are excluded.

results.question: What percentage of our revenue was refunded?
results.sql: WITH rev AS (SELECT sum(total) AS gross_revenue FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'), ref AS (SELECT sum(r.amount) AS total_refunds FROM refunds r JOIN orders o USING (order_id) WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided') SELECT round((ref.total_refunds / rev.gross_revenue) * 100, 2) AS refund_percentage, rev.gross_revenue, ref.total_refunds FROM rev, ref
results.answer: Your refunded revenue made up 3.51% of your total sales for all time. Specifically, you had $116,631.92 in refunds out of $3,321,930.71 in gross revenue. This calculation assumes all non-voided orders from October 1, 2025, through September 30, 2026.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: total refund amount divided by total gross revenue across all non-voided orders for all time (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).
